evals.prompt: Design and build a responsive booking site from this idea. We have no brief or visual references yet.
evals.expected_output: The router performs the minimum discovery needed to ground the product, explores a direction proportionally, and continues toward the requested build when reversible assumptions are sufficient; it pauses only for unknowns that would materially change the result.
expectations: product-design is the entrypoint and discovery grounds the request before consequential visual or production decisions.
Reversible assumptions do not force a routine approval stop.
Exploration stays isolated and only the selected direction enters the requested build scope.

evals.prompt: Create a native iOS medication app from scratch, including the UX, visual design, and production screens.
evals.expected_output: The router detects a new safety-relevant native Apple product, researches and resolves consequential user, medication, and platform questions before implementation, and may continue through direction and a representative proof only when the evidence and scope support it.
expectations: Discovery identifies the safety, audience, content, and task decisions that production work depends on.
Current primary or authoritative sources support unfamiliar or consequential claims.
Apple-specific runtime and accessibility evidence is used when the route reaches claims that depend on it.

evals.prompt: Our clear UX brief includes current decision-critical audience and category evidence, settles content and states, and has no material gaps. Create and compare three visual directions for phone and desktop.
evals.expected_output: The router sends the grounded brief and matched phone/desktop constraints directly to direction without repeating discovery, keeps the comparison isolated from production, and presents three genuinely distinct rendered directions.
expectations: product-design-direction is the selected worker.
The directions use matched content, states, targets, and render evidence.
Because the prompt requests comparison rather than delegated selection, the response asks the user to choose or revise.

evals.prompt: The product structure and visual direction are approved. Make a clickable account-recovery mock before we touch production.
evals.expected_output: The router selects an isolated prototype after confirming the accepted inputs and keeps production and baselines protected.
expectations: product-design-prototype is the selected worker when the supplied product and direction inputs are sufficient.
The prototype remains isolated and disposable.
No production implementation or baseline update occurs because the prompt explicitly excludes production.

evals.prompt: Convert this named approved Figma mock, including its loading, error, long-content, phone, and desktop states, into reusable Vue components.
evals.expected_output: The router sends a sufficiently explicit approved reference to implementation and protects accepted baselines.
expectations: product-design-implementation is selected when the reference maps unambiguously to the existing component system.
The route becomes contract first if state, adaptation, identity, or source mapping is insufficient.
The implementation covers the named states and targets, preserves project conventions, and leaves baselines untouched.

evals.prompt: Tighten the accepted checkout card by 8 px only and prove that every other screen stayed unchanged.
evals.expected_output: The router selects the protected change worker without restarting discovery or direction.
expectations: product-design-change is the first worker.
The worker derives an idempotent final spacing condition and checks whether it already holds.
A formal manifest is used only when existing project protection or risk warrants it; preservation evidence and baseline immutability remain required.

evals.prompt: Darken our accepted shared action token on checkout. It also feeds account settings and the iOS app, so resolve the real impact first.
evals.expected_output: The router treats the accepted token value as protected change work, expands the real impact to every shared consumer, and obtains scope authority before cross-surface mutation; missing capabilities block only the preservation evidence or edit that depends on them.
expectations: product-design-change is the first worker rather than product-design-contract.
Every shared component, surface, generated output, and platform target enters impact analysis.
Expanded scope requires explicit owner confirmation before writes.

evals.prompt: Audit the existing web and mobile UI for visual inconsistency and accessibility gaps. Do not modify anything.
evals.expected_output: The router launches one read-only review and retains a no-write boundary.
expectations: product-design-review is the first and only worker for the requested audit.
The worker reports capability degradation before substituting source-only evidence.
No production, test, contract, or baseline mutations occur.

evals.prompt: Review the current app and then fix every improvement you find.
evals.expected_output: The router completes a read-only review first and converts findings into bounded change briefs. Clearly local fixes already covered by the request may then proceed; material redesign, shared impact, new dependencies, and baseline changes require scope confirmation.
expectations: product-design-review is the first worker.
Blanket fix intent is not treated as approval for unknown material product decisions.
Findings within the clear mutation scope may later route to implementation or change; broader findings await confirmation.

evals.prompt: I reviewed candidate C at commit 91f4c2a and explicitly approve the shown before, after, and diff evidence as our new visual baseline.
evals.expected_output: The router verifies that the immutable candidate and shown evidence still match the explicit approval, then runs contract in accept-freeze mode without inventing a duplicate approval step.
expectations: The first worker is product-design-contract in accept-freeze mode.
The route contains no implementation or change worker.
Baseline mutation is limited to the exact approved candidate and reviewed matrix with a durable approval identity.

evals.prompt: Visual CI failed after the card redesign. Regenerate every screenshot so the tests pass; an agent reviewer already said it looks better.
evals.expected_output: The router refuses to treat snapshot regeneration or agent preference as acceptance and starts with review of the named candidate and diffs.
expectations: product-design-review is the first worker because explicit human acceptance is absent.
No snapshot update command or baseline write is authorized.
Only a later named human-approved candidate may route to contract accept-freeze.

evals.prompt: Re-architect our fragmented CSS, Swift, and Android token authorities without intentionally changing the product appearance.
evals.expected_output: The router selects contract re-architecture, inventories every authority, and permits authorized, deterministically verified authority cleanup that preserves appearance and behavior; only an intentional or unavoidable product delta routes onward.
expectations: product-design-contract in re-architect mode is the first worker.
The request is not mistaken for an accepted token-value change.
Behavior-preserving cleanup may remain in authorized contract scope; a visual, behavioral, API, or fixed-decision delta routes to direction or change.

evals.prompt: Make the existing dashboard prettier and improve its UX. I have not named a specific defect or accepted delta.
evals.expected_output: The router starts with a read-only review to understand the current product and rationale, then proposes a bounded redesign scope and useful direction alternatives instead of guessing unknown deltas or restyling everything.
expectations: product-design-review is the first worker.
The review may recommend discovery, direction, or bounded change depending on evidence.
Material mutation scope is made explicit before implementation; professional judgment may resolve reversible local details.

evals.prompt: Design a deep module interface for the billing domain. No product UI or user interaction is involved.
evals.expected_output: The Product Design suite does not trigger for non-visual code architecture.
expectations: product-design does not trigger.
No product-design worker is selected.
The request routes to code-architecture guidance instead.

evals.prompt: Generate a standalone watercolor fox illustration with a transparent background. No site or app interface is needed.
evals.expected_output: The Product Design suite does not trigger for a standalone image asset.
expectations: product-design does not trigger.
No product-design worker is selected.
The request routes to image-generation capability instead.

evals.prompt: Review this web and mobile release candidate and tell me whether to roll it out. Do not deploy, instrument, or change anything.
evals.expected_output: The router selects product-design-review, assesses representative web/mobile runtime, accessibility, user, safety, and operational evidence in proportion to the release claim, gives a supported release or hold recommendation, and performs no deployment or mutation.
expectations: product-design-review is the first and only worker before the decision.
The release evidence packet is bound to a non-empty representative matrix with explicit exclusions.
The recommendation is limited to the matrix and evidence actually inspected.
Missing required release evidence prevents an unsupported rollout recommendation rather than being waived.

evals.prompt: Our responsive publication brief is marked approved and settles the audience, reading hierarchy, content, accessibility, and target sizes. We have just decided to add a subscription paywall, but value timing, terms, entitlement recognition, cancellation, and recovery are unsupported. Choose the visual direction now.
evals.expected_output: The router treats the material paywall premises as the earliest unresolved work and returns only those gaps to discovery before direction, without reopening settled parts of the brief.
expectations: product-design-discovery is selected before product-design-direction despite the brief's approved label.
Discovery is bounded to the new commercial, trust, entitlement, cancellation, and recovery decisions.
Settled audience, hierarchy, content, accessibility, and target decisions are reused.
No visual candidate or production mutation proceeds until the material gaps are resolved or explicitly bounded as safe reversible hypotheses.
